[LRST.4.5] **An `after … as` clause supersedes its capture fact with its
timer.** The timer fact ([LTAC.3.2]) and the capture fact ([LTAC.3.5]) of one
`after` clause carry the same correlation — the clause's evaluated `as` key —
and a new activation with that key must retract both before asserting its own
pair. This is [LRST.4.1]'s rule for a `call`'s capture fact, on the clause that
carries the other kind of deferred body.

The pair is what makes it a rule of its own rather than a consequence of
[LRST.2.1]. Superseding the timer alone leaves the prior capture fact live on a
correlation the surviving follow-up joins, so one timer fires a body once per
capture snapshot ever taken under that key.

An `after` clause with no `as` supersedes nothing: its correlation is unique to
the activation ([LTAC.3.5]), so there is no prior pair to find.
